title: Late Breaking Results: Practical Electromagnetic Fault Injection on Intel Neural Compute Stick 2
problem: Edge ML devices deployed in critical IoT infrastructure lack empirical evaluation of physical fault injection vulnerability; security posture of real edge accelerators undefined.
motivation: Wide deployment of ML in critical infrastructures creates urgent need to evaluate practical security threats from low-cost electromagnetic fault injection attacks on edge ML hardware.
method: Conducts electromagnetic fault injection (EMFI) experiments on Intel Neural Compute Stick 2 using low-cost pulse generator hardware. Systematically varies EMFI fault parameters to induce misclassification at inference output, achieving repeatable results.
key_novelty: First practical demonstration of repeatable electromagnetic fault injection attacks causing misclassification on real Intel NCS2 edge ML accelerator.
contributions: Practical EMFI attack methodology on commercial edge ML device (NCS2)
Low-cost attack setup achieving repeatable misclassifications
Empirical characterization of fault parameter space for edge ML inference
baselines: previous fault injection studies on other devices
limitations: Limited to single device type (NCS2); mitigation strategies not proposed; generalization to other edge accelerators not addressed.
primary_theme: physical fault injection vulnerability in edge ML accelerators
